brief.whatItIs: Score-impact skill: choose and interpret summary statistics based on what they measure and whether they resist outliers. Mean and standard deviation are sensitive; median and IQR are resistant.
brief.whyItMatters: The reason this skill matters here is that a correct calculation is not enough if the answer does not label the statistic and explain what it means for the data.
brief.howPointsAreEarned: A strong answer names the statistic, shows or states the relevant value, labels the variable and units, and explains why that statistic fits the distribution or question.
brief.answerMove: Open hand: ask, "Am I describing center, spread, position, or outliers, and which statistic does that job?"
brief.commonPointLoss: Reporting a summary number without labeling what it summarizes, or using a nonresistant statistic when the question calls attention to outliers or skew.

explainer.coreIdea: The score-impact move is choosing the statistic that matches the job: center, spread, position, or resistance to outliers.
explainer.whatStudentsNeedToUnderstand: Summary statistics are point-earning only when the student labels what they summarize and interprets them with units and context.
explainer.howThisBecomesPoints: Students protect points by showing the value, naming the statistic, including units when available, and explaining why that statistic fits the distribution or question.
explainer.answerMove: Open hand: ask, "Am I describing center, spread, position, or outliers, and which statistic does that job?"
explainer.miniExampleQuestion: A dataset of home prices has one extremely expensive house. Which center should a student report for a typical price?
explainer.weakAnswer: Use the mean because it uses all the numbers.
explainer.pointAttainingAnswer: Use the median to describe a typical price because it is resistant to the extremely expensive house. The mean would be pulled upward by the outlier.
explainer.commonPointLoss: Reporting a summary number without labeling what it summarizes, or using a nonresistant statistic when the question calls attention to outliers or skew.
explainer.practiceBridge: When outliers are present, ask whether the question wants a resistant summary before choosing mean or median.

wordingCorrections: Use the sample formula with denominator n - 1 when defining sample variance; avoid calling it simply the average squared deviation.

topicSummary.label: Topic summary
topicSummary.title: Summary Statistics
topicSummary.body: Choose center or spread, then check whether outliers call for a resistant measure.

primaryAnswerMove.label: Primary answer move
primaryAnswerMove.body: Name the statistic and value with units. Explain why it fits the distribution.

coreIdea.label: Deep Dive
coreIdea.title: Match the statistic to the job
paragraphs: Summary statistics describe center, spread, position, and unusual values. Choose one that matches the question.
Mean and standard deviation are sensitive to extremes. Median and IQR resist them and often fit skewed data better.

topicFormulaReference.label: New in 1.7

items.explanation: Mean: center using every observed value.
IQR: resistant spread of the middle 50%.

topicFormulaReference.unitBoundary: The complete formula collection remains unit-owned.

answerSteps.label: Answer move
answerSteps.title: Turn a calculated value into a complete statistical answer

steps.title: Name the job
steps.body: Decide whether the prompt asks about center, spread, position, outliers, or resistance.

steps.title: Choose and report
steps.body: Name the statistic, show or state its value, and include units when they are available.

steps.title: Justify the fit
steps.body: Explain why the statistic suits the distribution, especially when skew or outliers affect resistance.

items.mistake: Reports a summary number without naming what it summarizes.
items.correction: Name the statistic, variable, value, and units.

items.mistake: Uses a nonresistant statistic when skew or outliers matter.
items.correction: Check whether median or IQR better matches the question.

workedExample.label: Worked example
workedExample.title: Choose a typical value when one home price is extreme
workedExample.prompt: A dataset of home prices contains one extremely expensive house. Which measure of center should a student report to describe a typical home price?

weakResponse.title: Ignores resistance
weakResponse.body: Use the mean because it uses all the numbers.

strongerResponse.title: Matches statistic to distribution
strongerResponse.body: Use the median because it is resistant to the extremely expensive house. The mean would be pulled upward by that outlier.

workedExample.whyItWorks: It names the median, links resistance to the outlier, and explains why the mean would be misleading.
workedExample.review: SME review for example; Learning Quality for whyItWorks

practiceBridge.label: Before practice
practiceBridge.body: Before choosing a statistic, ask: What job must it do, and does the distribution call for resistance?
